# Results — Study 279 (Geomagnetic-Storms) on ^GSPC monthly price returns

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The geomagnetic Ap index is
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../geomagnetic_storms/data.py) (deterministic, 1932–2025). ^GSPC
monthly **price** returns are resampled from the cached daily series
(`_cache/^GSPC_split_only.parquet`). Match the fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same
data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC monthly price return (cache, month-end resample) | 1932–2025 | 1,128 months | `4be838e7a71e` |
| Geomagnetic Ap index | 1932–2025 | 1,128 months | hardcoded constant |

Regime split (top/bottom quintile of Ap): **226 stormy**, **226 calm**, **676 normal**.
Ap thresholds: calm ≤ **11.6**, stormy ≥ **28.5**.

## The headline: calm vs stormy months

| Regime | n months | mean return (%/month) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Calm (bottom quintile Ap) | 226 | **+1.219%** |
| Normal (middle 60%) | 676 | +0.661% |
| Stormy (top quintile Ap) | 226 | **+0.440%** |

- **Calm-minus-stormy gap: +0.78%/month** (~**+9.3%/yr**) — the right sign: storms precede
  lower returns, exactly as Krivelyova-Robotti predict.
- **Newey-West HAC t-stat (the honest one): +1.88** — just below the |t| = 2 desk bar. Both
  storms (solar-cycle bursts) and returns cluster in time, so the HAC SE is larger than the
  naive one; this is the conservative, correct read.
- **Welch two-sample t: +1.68** (p = 0.094) — same story, treating months as independent.
- **Permutation p (10,000 shuffles, one-sided): 0.046** — clears 0.05, but the permutation
  test assumes exchangeable months and so over-credits the effect relative to the HAC t.

## Sub-period robustness

| Period | n | gap (%/month) | HAC t | perm p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1932–1979 | 576 | +0.932 | +1.60 | 0.099 |
| 1980–2025 | 552 | +0.690 | +1.18 | 0.133 |
| 1990–2025 | 432 | +1.052 | +1.83 | 0.059 |

The gap is the **right sign in every sub-period** (a genuine point in favour), but the HAC
t-stat is **below 2.0 in every sub-period**. Directionally persistent, statistically
borderline — the signature of a *Weak*, not *Real*, effect.

## The tradable overlay (long-calm / short-storm, 1-month lag, costs + borrow)

| Strategy | ann. return | HAC t | Sharpe (ann.) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Storm overlay — gross | +2.82% | +2.26 | — |
| Storm overlay — net | +2.41% | +1.92 | 0.22 |
| Buy & hold ^GSPC | +8.74% | — | 0.49 |

- Even **gross**, the overlay earns only +2.8%/yr — the calm-month bias is real but small, and
  the strategy is **flat ~60% of months** (it acts only after a stormy or calm month).
- **Net** of one-way costs (10 bps × NAV on each position change) and short borrow (8 bps/month),
  it earns +2.4%/yr — a fraction of buy-and-hold. Average monthly cost drag: **3.45 bps**.
- Sitting flat or short through a nine-decade bull market is the killer. **No tradable edge.**

## Positive control (synthetic)

Planting a known per-month storm penalty in a synthetic tape and measuring the HAC t-stat:

| Planted penalty (bps/month) | gap (%/month) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 (null) | ~0.00 | ~0.1 |
| 60 | ~0.6 | > 2 |
| 200 | ~2.0 | > 5 |

The machinery is honest: a null gives t ≈ 0, a real penalty pushes t well past 2. The real
^GSPC tape sits at **1.88** — the method is not the bottleneck; the signal is simply thin.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Gap +0.78%/month (right sign, ~9%/yr), perm p = 0.046, with a published
  mood mechanism — but Newey-West HAC t = **1.88** (< 2.0) and < 2.0 in every sub-period. The
  desk bar for a REAL stamp is a robust |t| ≥ 2 on the real tape; literature support and the
  correct sign earn WEAK, not Real.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only implementable version (lagged long-calm / short-storm)
  earns +2.4%/yr net (Sharpe 0.22) vs +8.7%/yr buy-and-hold (Sharpe 0.49). No edge survives
  costs, borrow, and the opportunity cost of stepping out of the drift.
- **Caveats (on the Signal axis):** ^GSPC is **price-only** (dividends would lift the drift and
  hurt the short leg further — the real shortfall is worse); storm/calm thresholds are
  **in-sample** (a mild look-ahead that flatters the gap).
